title: Synergistic degradation of fucoidans in the ocean.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Zenodo record 19591477 (CC-BY-4.0, licence that allows reuse with credit): listed 7 files. Opened motus.fucoidan_degraders.summary.tsv.gz (1,632 rows x 11 columns: mOTU species-cluster ID, fucoidanase gene count, gene types, PUL (polysaccharide utilisation locus) count, GTDB (Genome Taxonomy Database) taxonomy) and isolates.env_samples_detected.tsv.gz (68,221 rows: isolate, source, sample, lat/lon, match type). GitHub repo holds only README plus scripts.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Experimental design, read from the bioRxiv preprint 2025.08.13.670036: 87 pairwise co-cultures, 127 combinations of up to 7 degraders, 63 community-substrate combinations across 9 fucoidans (277 configurations, 3 replicates each), degradation measured by LC-MS (liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry) as % of monomers released. The paper's own Hill-function model reaches R2 0.96 (in-sample) and 0.87 (out-of-sample). Those tables are in the Nature Supplementary Information, which has no PMCID and was not opened.

a1_downloadable.note: Zenodo metagenome tables download openly (checked). The experimental degradation tables sit only in the Nature supplement (no PMC copy), so they were not retrieved.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Per the preprint, degradation % per community is a measured value, presumably in a column of the supplement. Not seen in the files.

a3_inputs_present.note: For the experimental task the inputs are which strains are present plus substrate identity, a small presence/absence design (paper text only).

a4_units_stated.note: Preprint states % of monomers released and consumed, measured by LC-MS. Not checked in the files.

a5_enough_rows.note: The measured data covers only 277 community configurations (87 pairs + 127 multi-member + 63 substrate combos, per the preprint), under the ~400 needed even for classification. The 1,632-row Zenodo table has no measured label.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Zenodo summary has 1,632 mOTU species clusters. The paper's count of predicted degraders was not available to compare against.

a8_label_provenance.note: In the open Zenodo tables, 'fucoidan degrader' is defined as at least 5 fucoidanase genes (Zenodo description, Fucoidanase_gene_count column), so the label is computed from the gene-annotation features themselves.

existing_models.name: Paper's own trait-based Hill-function model (strain capacities for fucose vs rare-sugar pools)
existing_models.score_and_split: R2 0.96 on 127 community combinations; R2 0.87 on out-of-sample substrate predictions across 9 fucoidans (bioRxiv preprint).

backbone.name: ESM-2 (protein language model) could embed fucoidanase sequences from the Zenodo FASTA, but there is no measured activity label to train against

integration.partner_dataset: CAZy (carbohydrate-active enzyme database) families / mOTUs community profiles
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Which ocean regions host complementary fucoidan degraders. But that is answered by counting co-occurrence, not by a learned model.

controls.positive_control: Recover the paper's two guilds (fucose-backbone vs rare-sugar degraders) from strain-presence weights.
controls.external_validation: None; one consortium from one coastal site.

honest_claim_h3: Predicts how much of one of 9 fucoidans a mix drawn from about 7 lab isolates degrades, which a 2-parameter-per-strain mechanistic model already does with R2 0.87.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use which bacterial strains are mixed together, and which algal sugar they get, to predict how much of the sugar gets broken down.
plain_idea.train_on: Strain presence/absence plus substrate identity for 277 community setups (count from the preprint, not from the files).
plain_idea.predict: Percent of fucoidan sugar units released and consumed, measured by LC-MS (liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry) in triplicate cultures.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: It would guide which strain mixes to build for breaking down tough polysaccharides, but the authors' simple mechanistic model already explains 87-96% of the variation.

more_or_better_data.why: We would use the same 277 configurations the authors' model was fit on; no extra data.

confidence_score.why: Triplicates allow noise estimates, but the authors' fit is already close to that ceiling.

models_beatable.why: The 2026 mechanistic Hill model reaches R2 0.87 on held-out substrates with few parameters, leaving little room.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No second dataset measures degradation of the same strains the same way.

ml_idea: Predict consortium degradation efficiency from strain presence and substrate: too few rows (277), and a mechanistic model already fits at R2 0.87-0.96. The open metagenomic tables label degraders by gene count, so that label is circular.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; rejected at Part A.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count rows in the Nature supplementary degradation table. The preprint implies about 277, which is below the bar.

verdict_reason: A5: only about 277 measured community configurations (preprint count; the Nature supplement was not opened), and the authors' own mechanistic model already reaches R2 0.87 out-of-sample. A8: the open Zenodo 'degrader' label is defined as at least 5 fucoidanase genes, so it is computed from the features.
